title: GREYHOUND: Hunting Fail-Slows in Hybrid-Parallel Training at Scale
problem: Fail-slows (stragglers) are transient slowdowns in large-scale hybrid-parallel GPU training lasting from sub-minutes to nearly ten hours, caused by slow computations or communications due to contention, device degradation, or network congestion. Current manual detection and checkpoint-restart failover approaches are time-consuming and ineffective.
motivation: Fail-slows are prevalent in production GPU clusters and delay large training jobs by 1.34x on average, necessitating automatic detection and mitigation at scale.
method: GREYHOUND automatically identifies slow GPUs and communication links through a detection mechanism achieving >99% accuracy. It applies a novel multi-level mitigation strategy to address identified stragglers without human intervention or checkpoint-restart overhead. The system monitors during hybrid-parallel training and adaptively responds to detected slowdowns.
key_novelty: An automated multi-level mitigation mechanism that handles stragglers without requiring checkpoint-restart failover or manual operator intervention.
contributions: Characterization of fail-slows in production GPU clusters with 10,000+ GPUs, quantifying impact (1.34x slowdown) and temporal patterns
Automated detection system achieving >99% accuracy for slow GPUs and communication links
Novel multi-level mitigation strategy integrated into hybrid-parallel training framework
1.58x end-to-end throughput improvement on 256 H800 GPUs with automatic straggler handling
limitations: Paper does not discuss limitations in the abstract.
primary_theme: automated fail-slow detection and mitigation in hybrid-parallel training
